label: Geneva — UN Mediation Hub
sub: Headquarters of OHCHR, UNHCR, UNOG, and dozens of peace processes including Syria, Yemen, Libya consultations. Annual Human Rights Council sessions.

label: Oslo — Oslo Accords (1993)
sub: Secret back-channel talks hosted by Norway's FAFO Institute led to the Israel–PLO Declaration of Principles signed Sep 13, 1993. Norway continues as peace mediator in Colombia (ELN/FARC) and other contexts.

label: Doha — Peace Talks Hub
sub: Host of U.S.–Taliban Doha Agreement (Feb 2020), Gaza ceasefire negotiations (2023–26), Sudan peace consultations, and Afghan intra-dialogue. Qatar's mediation role is central to multiple active processes.

label: Belfast — Good Friday Agreement (1998)
sub: The Belfast Agreement of April 10, 1998 ended 30 years of 'The Troubles'. Northern Ireland's power-sharing institutions remain the model for consociational peace. Brexit tensions test the agreement's Irish dimension.

label: Dayton — Bosnia Peace Accords (1995)
sub: The General Framework Agreement for Peace in Bosnia was initialed at Wright-Patterson AFB on Nov 21, 1995, ending the Bosnian War. Created Bosnia's two-entity structure under a unified state. NATO IFOR/SFOR enforced peace.

label: Bogotá — De la Espriella Extradites Total Peace Negotiators, Ends Policy
sub: Final peace agreement with FARC-EP signed Nov 24, 2016. JEP continues operating here. AUG 7 — De la Espriella inaugurated after winning the runoff; branded Total Peace 'fake peace' and began revoking benefits negotiated under Petro, reviewing prior commitments, and reactivating arrest warrants. Launched a 90-day 'shock plan' (aerial bombardment, forced coca eradication) that as of Aug 19 amounts to Colombia's largest offensive against armed groups in a decade. Former combatants in government-recognized demobilization zones (ZUTs) await word on whether prior agreements will be honored; ELN talks remain suspended, FARC dissidents fragmented (Mordisco rearmed; Calarcá faction maintains separate dialogue). AUG 27 — De la Espriella formalized Total Peace's end, ordering the extradition to the US of five individuals recognized as negotiators in the prior government's talks (FARC dissident, ELN dissident and Los Pachenca/ACSN figures), declaring 'In my government, there will be no peace processes.'

label: Havana — Colombia Peace Talks Venue
sub: Cuba hosted FARC–government talks 2012–2016 and continues as guarantor for ELN negotiations under Petro's Total Peace framework. Joint guarantor with Norway. ELN talks suspended since January 2025 Catatumbo massacre.

label: Addis Ababa — African Union HQ
sub: African Union Commission headquarters. Hub for IGAD, AUHIP (Sudan), AU peace missions. Hosted Ethiopia–Tigray Pretoria Agreement (2022) implementation monitoring. Key venue for Horn of Africa peace diplomacy.

label: Nairobi — IGAD / EAC Peace Hub
sub: Hosted Sudan CPA signing (2005), South Sudan R-ARCSS follow-on talks, and DRC–Rwanda Nairobi Track negotiations. IGAD headquarters. Kenya's Uhuru Kenyatta mediated Ethiopia–Tigray Pretoria process. RSF's Hemeti in Apr 2026 Nairobi talks with UN envoy Haavisto.

label: Pretoria — Ethiopia–Tigray Agreement (2022)
sub: Cessation of Hostilities Agreement signed Nov 2, 2022, ending 2 years of devastating war. AU-mediated by Obasanjo, Kenyatta, Mlambo-Ngcuka. Most significant African peace deal of the 2020s.

label: Jeddah — Sudan Peace Platform
sub: U.S.–Saudi Arabia jointly host Jeddah talks between SAF and RSF since May 2023. Multiple ceasefire declarations signed here have collapsed within hours. US Adviser Boulos presented five-pillar peace roadmap on Sudan's 3-year anniversary, April 15, 2026.

label: Stockholm — Yemen Hodeidah Agreement (2018)
sub: UN-brokered Stockholm Agreement of Dec 13, 2018 includes Hodeidah port ceasefire and prisoner exchange framework. UN Mission to support the Hodeidah Agreement (UNMHA) monitors ceasefire. Prevented catastrophic battle for Yemen's main supply port.

label: Minsk — Ukraine–Russia (Minsk I & II)
sub: Minsk Protocol (Sep 2014) and Minsk II (Feb 2015) established ceasefire and political roadmap for Donbas. OSCE monitored compliance. Russia's 2022 full invasion rendered the Minsk framework defunct. Both parties dispute who negotiated in bad faith.

label: Kyiv — Witkoff, Kushner Shuttle Diplomacy Continues; No Ceasefire
sub: Russia's Feb 24, 2022 invasion. Diplomatic track frozen since Russia's Jun 7 dismissal of Zelensky's open letter ('come to Moscow'). AUG 2026: Zelensky says Kyiv and partners developed a pressure-based plan against Putin (Aug 12); US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner prepare renewed shuttle trips to Kyiv and Moscow through August, but no breakthrough format has been finalized. Russia continues to insist on full Donbas cession; Ukraine rejects unilateral withdrawal and demands negotiations based on the line of contact. Front line remains the core sticking point alongside security guarantees; no ceasefire framework in force.

label: Gaza — Board of Peace Warns of 'Point of No Return'
sub: Ceasefire nominally in force since Oct 10, 2025 but Israeli strikes have killed 1,200+ Palestinians since then. Netanyahu formally rejected the Board of Peace's 15-point roadmap Aug 9, insisting on Hamas disarmament before any IDF withdrawal. AUG 17 — Kushner and Netanyahu agreed a US general (Maj. Gen. Jasper Jeffers, ISF) will oversee a Hamas weapons handover to a proposed technocratic committee (NCAG) and the ISF, following rare direct Board of Peace-Hamas talks in Egypt. AUG 18 — an Israeli strike on alleged Hamas commanders killed 6 in Gaza City one day after Kushner urged restraint. AUG 23 — two Israeli strikes killed 3 more Palestinians, and Netanyahu/Katz threatened to 'intensify strikes' over kite/balloon launches, which Hamas called a fabricated pretext. AUG 25 — in a rare public rebuke to both sides, a Board of Peace official told Reuters 'all militant activity in Gaza must stop, including the flying of kites,' but also warned Israel that 'military action cannot extend beyond responding to genuine and imminent threats,' as Gaza's popular committees urged parents to stop children flying kites. AUG 26 — Board of Peace chair Nikolay Mladenov told the UN Security Council a ceasefire collapse would be an irreversible 'point of no return,' crediting Hamas's first-ever agreement to hand over weapons and governing authority while also criticizing Israel's continued strikes. The disarmament-before-withdrawal vs. withdrawal-before-disarmament impasse remains unresolved.

label: Khartoum — Anti-War Forces Reject Burhan Dialogue, Propose Alternative Roadmap
sub: SAF vs RSF conflict erupted Apr 15, 2023; 150,000+ killed, 14M displaced, famine in Darfur. US-brokered Boulos peace-roadmap talks remain stalled (SAF/RSF gave incompatible responses Jul 12-14). AUG 15 — Burhan pledged temporary immunity and legal guarantees for participants in a proposed national dialogue but ruled out any political comeback for RSF's Hemedti. AUG 15-16 — an AU Peace and Security Council delegation (15 member states, led by Algeria) made its first Khartoum-based visit since the war began, meeting Burhan and PM Kamil Idris and welcoming steps toward reopening the AU's Khartoum liaison office. AUG 20 — PM Al-Ta'aishi urged the AU PSC toward impartiality as Khartoum and Riyadh established a bilateral coordination council. AUG 22-23 — a broad anti-war civilian/political coalition (Sumoud, Popular Congress Party, Umma Party faction, civil society) met in Addis Ababa and formally rejected Burhan's dialogue offer as a manoeuvre to entrench military rule, adopting an alternative "Peace Process We Want" roadmap built on humanitarian access, a permanent ceasefire, and an exclusively civilian transition.

label: Goma — DRC M23/Rwanda: M23 Withdraws from Ruzizi Plain (South Kivu) — First Territorial Concession Since Washington Accords
sub: M23 rebels captured Goma Jan 27, 2025. Washington Accords (Dec 2025) implementation underway: 5th JOC met Apr 23; DRC National Assembly ratification bills adopted Apr 28 (to Senate). KEY UPDATE May 14-17: M23 withdrew unilaterally from the Ruzizi Plain in South Kivu — the first territorial concession since December 2025 accords. Qatar-mediated Doha process (DRC-AFC/M23) continues alongside Washington framework. FDLR not disbanded; Rwanda assessed 'deeply disappointing' by US; COVM verification active; 7M+ still displaced in eastern DRC.

label: Cotabato — Bangsamoro Peace (Philippines)
sub: Capital of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), established 2019 under the Bangsamoro Organic Law. MILF decommissioning proceeds in phases. BIFF and Abu Sayyaf remain spoilers.

label: Freetown — Sierra Leone Post-Conflict TJ
sub: Special Court for Sierra Leone operated 2002–2013, convicting Charles Taylor (in absentia) and RUF leaders. Truth and Reconciliation Commission completed its work 2004. Sierra Leone recovery model cited as post-conflict success despite ongoing governance challenges.

label: Bogotá — Colombia JEP (Transitional Justice)
sub: Colombia's Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) investigates war crimes by FARC and military. Macro-case 01 examines 6,402+ cases of 'false positives' (civilians killed by army and registered as combatants). Colombia's TJ model is the most advanced in the Americas.

label: Banda Aceh — Helsinki MOU (2005)
sub: Post-tsunami peace breakthrough: Helsinki MOU ended 29-year GAM insurgency. EU and ASEAN monitoring mission verified demobilization. Aceh given special autonomy and oil revenue sharing. Considered a landmark post-disaster peace opportunity.

label: Mogadishu — Somalia Reconciliation
sub: AU Mission in Somalia (AMISOM/ATMIS) and UN Assistance Mission (UNSOM) support federal reconciliation process. Clan-based power sharing (4.5 formula) underpins government formation. Al-Shabaab controls 20%+ of territory. National Consultative Council attempts to resolve federal-state disputes.

label: Tripoli — Libya Peace Process
sub: Government of National Unity (GNU) recognized by UN but contested by Benghazi-based government. Libya Political Dialogue Forum (LPDF) attempts to bridge east-west divide. Ceasefire signed Oct 2020 broadly holds but elections remain blocked since Dec 2021. Turkey and UAE/Egypt back competing factions.

label: Nicosia — Cyprus Reunification Talks
sub: UN-mediated talks on bizonal bicommunal federation have continued since 1974 Turkish intervention. Most recent formal talks at Crans-Montana 2017 collapsed. UN Special Adviser Jane Holl Lute conducts informal consultations. Divided capital remains last divided city in EU-candidate zone.

label: Kathmandu — Nepal Transitional Justice
sub: Nepal's Truth and Reconciliation Commission and Commission on Enforced Disappearances were established under the 2014 TRC Act but stalled repeatedly. A landmark Supreme Court ruling 2024 requires accountability for conflict-era crimes. Nepal's TJ process is one of the world's longest-stalled.

label: Islamabad — Pakistan Reports 'Significant Progress' Reviving Lapsed MOU
sub: Pakistan hosted Round 1 of US–Iran talks April 11–12 (collapsed); the June 17, 2026 Islamabad MOU later opened a 60-day negotiating window on Hormuz navigation, sanctions, and the nuclear program. AUG 12 — Pakistan mounted a final diplomatic push (Dep. PM Dar, Interior Min. Naqvi to Tehran) ahead of the deadline. AUG 17 — the 60-day window expired without a comprehensive agreement. AUG 20 — Trump announced an 'economic D-Day' sanctions threat; Iran's Araghchi rejected it as a 'diversion.' AUG 24-25 — Pakistan's army chief Munir and Interior Min. Naqvi made a daylong mission to Tehran, meeting Pezeshkian, Araghchi and Rezaei; Naqvi called the talks 'highly positive' and said both sides reviewed steps to restore the MOU, though Pezeshkian said 'the United States must correct its tone and approach.' Any extension requires mutual consent; none formally announced yet. India-Pakistan LoC ceasefire (1-year mark May 10) continues holding separately, with no formal peace framework.

label: India–Pakistan LoC — Operation Sindoor Ceasefire (1-Year Anniversary)
sub: May 10, 2026: One-year anniversary of the India–Pakistan ceasefire that ended Operation Sindoor (May 7–10, 2025). India struck nine alleged terror camps in Pakistan/PoK following the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam attack (26 killed). Ceasefire announced by US Secretary Rubio; India describes it as bilateral. One year on: ceasefire holding but Indus Waters Treaty suspended, trade severed, diplomatic ties downgraded, both sides on high alert. No formal normalization or peace process framework established. Al Jazeera: 'rising risks and deepening instability' despite ceasefire. Trump nominated for Nobel Peace Prize by Pakistan for brokering the truce. No formal peace talks or confidence-building measures launched.

label: Washington DC — Round 4 Joint Statement (Jun 3): Conditional Ceasefire + Pilot Zones Agreed; Hezbollah Rejects Jun 4
sub: U.S.-facilitated Washington Accords (DRC–Rwanda) signed Dec 4, 2025; 5th JOC met Apr 23, 2026. LEBANON-ISRAEL ROUND 4 (JUN 2–3): Pentagon joined talks for first time; joint US-Lebanon-Israel statement issued Jun 3 — conditional ceasefire framework, 'pilot zones' (LAF exclusive control, Hezbollah excluded), mutual non-hostility declaration, Round 5 set for June 22. JUN 4: Hezbollah SG Qassem publicly rejected the deal as 'absurd, humiliating, shameful' — fresh strikes exchanged; IDF operations continue. Iran: deal still unsigned Week 15; VP Vance: 'unclear if or when Trump signs.' Colombia: runoff Cepeda vs. De la Espriella June 21.

label: Beirut — Verification-Country Shortlist Disputed After Rome Round 7
sub: US-brokered ceasefire framework began Apr 16, 2026; Jun 26 Washington deal links progressive Israeli withdrawal to verified Hezbollah disarmament. The 7th round of Rome talks (Aug 4-7) reportedly produced a shortlist of countries (Britain, Italy, Switzerland, Indonesia) that could send troops to verify disarmament — with France vetoed by Israel/US — but a Lebanese official denied Aug 13 that Beirut had agreed to any such shortlist, saying Beirut was still following up with Washington. Hezbollah, not a party to the agreement, continues to refuse disarming. Next round of talks expected early September.

label: Cairo — Hamas Delegation for Phase 2 Talks (Jun 5-6)
sub: Egypt's intelligence chief Abbas Kamel hosted Hamas delegation led by Khalil Al-Hayya on June 5-6 for renewed Gaza Phase 2 ceasefire negotiations. Focus: addressing Phase 1 violations (3,005+) and reviving stalled Phase 2 framework (Israeli withdrawal from Gaza + Hamas disarmament). No breakthrough announced; both Egypt and Qatar described talks as 'constructive'. Core impasse: Hamas conditions disarmament on Palestinian statehood guarantee; Israel refuses. National Transitional Committee (Ali Shaath) continues as parallel governance track in Gaza.

label: Strait of Hormuz — Still Closed as 60-Day MOU Window Lapses Aug 17
sub: Critical maritime chokepoint — ~20% of global oil trade. Iran closed the Strait March 2026; hundreds of vessels affected; Iranian oil export revenue blocked. The Jun 17 Islamabad MOU set a 60-day window (Phase 1: Hormuz reopens, US blockade lifted, Iran oil sales resume; Phase 2: nuclear talks) that expired Aug 17 without resolution. Iran struck vessels it said deviated from its approved transit route; Iran's security chief said Hormuz 'will not reopen until the US ends the war and blockade, releases Iran's frozen assets, and agrees to a region-wide ceasefire,' while Washington separately demanded compensation for alleged decades of Iranian actions (Aug 11). No extension has been announced.

label: Cebu — 48th ASEAN Summit (May 5–9, 2026)
sub: The Philippines hosted the 48th ASEAN Summit in Cebu, May 5–9, 2026. Myanmar dominated regional diplomacy — five years after the Five-Point Consensus, ASEAN agreed only to schedule a virtual FM meeting with Myanmar's foreign minister. Min Aung Hlaing excluded from leader-level meetings. Summit also addressed Iran war's impact on ASEAN energy security. Outcome: 'tiny shifts' on Myanmar, no enforcement mechanisms created. Timor-Leste (Myanmar coordination chair) and Thailand sought to build diplomatic momentum. Summit statement reaffirmed Five-Point Consensus. Next key date: scheduled virtual ASEAN-Myanmar FM meeting.

label: Naypyidaw — Myanmar Junta; ASEAN Five-Point Consensus Fails at 5-Year Mark
sub: Myanmar's SAC junta (Min Aung Hlaing, sworn in as president April 2026) offered 100-day peace talks April 21; NUG and all EAOs rejected. SAC ceasefire expired April 30. 48th ASEAN Summit (Cebu, May 5–9) produced only 'tiny shifts' — no enforcement, Five-Point Consensus reaches 5-year anniversary of total non-compliance. May 12: Myanmar junta foreign ministry publicly complained of 'discriminatory measures' and 'pariah treatment' in ASEAN — frustration with post-summit isolation after being excluded from leader meetings. ASEAN SG announced virtual FM meeting 'in the near future' (no date). ASEAN deeply divided: Malaysia/Indonesia/Singapore maintain pressure on atrocity accountability; Thailand/Cambodia/Laos favor re-engagement. Myanmar has 3.3M+ IDPs.

label: Istanbul — Round 2 (Jun 2): 1,200-for-1,200 POW Exchange Agreed; Ukraine Full Ceasefire Proposal Rejected; No Ceasefire
sub: May 15–16, 2026: Istanbul hosted Ukraine-Russia Round 1 (collapsed; Putin absent) and Iran-EU3 nuclear talks. JUNE 2 — ROUND 2 COMPLETED: Sessions lasted ~1 hour. Key outcome: 1,200-for-1,200 POW exchange agreed in principle (severely injured soldiers, under-25 POWs, journalists, civilian political prisoners). Ukraine proposed: unconditional full ceasefire, all-for-all POW exchange, abducted children return, civilian release. Russia rejected unconditional ceasefire — countered with limited 2-3 day operational pause in specific front sectors only. Core territorial gap unbridged: Ukraine refuses cede territory; Russia insists ceasefire begin from occupation lines. Zelensky accused Russia Jun 2 of 'dragging out' the process. Jun 4: Zelensky published open letter to Putin proposing direct face-to-face talks in Switzerland, Turkey, or Arab state. Round 3 has no confirmed date.

label: Qamishli — SDF Formally Dissolves After Army Merger Complete
sub: AUG 20, 2026 — SDF commander Mazloum Abdi announced completion of Kurdish-led military, security, and administrative integration into Syrian state institutions, implementing the Jan 29, 2026 Damascus-SDF agreement. AUG 25 — Abdi announced the SDF's formal dissolution as an independent military force, declaring 'the end of the SDF's mission' now that Syria has 'entered a new phase, one of peace.' The merger deal formalizes recognition of Kurdish cultural, civil and educational rights, including Kurdish as a national language, Nowruz as an official holiday, and citizenship for previously stateless Kurds; Kurdish constitutional rights remain the next 'political battle.'

label: Caracas — 1,046+ Prisoners Freed Amid Reconciliation Process
sub: US-backed government-opposition talks began Aug 6-7, 2026 (government led by Jorge Rodríguez, opposition by Dinorah Figuera; María Corina Machado's bloc not participating). First round concluded Aug 12 with agreements on judicial reform and recovery of gold reserves frozen at the Bank of England for earthquake reconstruction. AUG 14-15 — the interim government freed 131 more people under the 'Program for Peace and Democratic Coexistence,' bringing the total freed since Jan 3 to 1,046+; Foro Penal confirmed at least 40 were political prisoners and estimates ~391 remain incarcerated. Rubio called the releases 'a crucial step for the nation's reconciliation process.'
